title: How a RAG Chatbot Answers From Your Docs

sections.heading: An everyday analogy
sections.body: Imagine a librarian for your docs. You ask a question, the librarian finds the right pages and writes an answer using only those pages. In Obelisk, that librarian is a RAG pipeline. RAG means Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Retrieval means finding relevant text. Generation means writing an answer with a language model, which is software that writes text like a person.

sections.heading: Why it exists
sections.body: A language model alone can guess and miss your private docs. RAG adds context. Document indexing splits docs into chunks, small pieces of text. Each chunk becomes a vector embedding, a list of numbers that captures meaning. These are saved in vector storage, a searchable shelf for meanings, using ChromaDB. Your question also becomes a vector to find close chunks. Those chunks plus the question go to the model, which can run locally via Ollama, a tool that runs models on your machine, or via an OpenAI-compatible API, a standard way for apps to talk to models.

sections.heading: What can go wrong
sections.body: If indexing is poor, wrong pages are found. If embeddings are weak, search fails. Without document monitoring, which means watching files and re-indexing when they change, answers use old info. At 100x usage, vector search slows and the local Ollama model can overload.

steps.narration: Start with your MkDocs docs as the source of truth.
Split docs into chunks and turn each into a vector embedding.
Save vectors in ChromaDB for fast meaning-based search.
Turn the user question into a vector too.
Find the closest doc vectors to get relevant context.
Give question plus context to Ollama to write a grounded answer.

quiz.q: What does RAG do in Obelisk?
options: It finds relevant docs first, then writes an answer using them
It trains a new model from scratch on your docs
It deletes old docs to save space
It only calls an external API with no retrieval
quiz.why: RAG is Retrieval-Augmented Generation: retrieve context, then generate.

quiz.q: What is a vector embedding here?
options: A list of numbers that captures the meaning of text
A copy of the original PDF
quiz.why: Embeddings let the system compare meaning by comparing numbers.

quiz.q: What fails first if usage grows 100x?
options: ChromaDB search slows and Ollama gets overloaded, causing slow or failed answers
MkDocs automatically rewrites all docs correctly
Embeddings become more accurate for free
quiz.why: More queries stress vector search, storage, and local generation.
